questions.q: Two high-speed trains collided near the town of Urda on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people. In which country?
questions.f: A Renfe train hit a stationary Iryo train in Toledo province, south of Madrid, and the nation declared official mourning.

questions.q: Cyclone Arnab crossed the coast on Wednesday after nearly 100,000 people were evacuated. Which country did it hit?
questions.f: The very severe cyclonic storm made landfall in Andhra Pradesh, with Odisha also evacuating residents.

questions.q: Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 10,000 confirmed cases this week. Which rare species of Ebola virus is driving it?
questions.f: The outbreak, announced in mid-May, has been linked to almost 4,900 deaths.

questions.q: Which nuclear watchdog chief told the UN Security Council there's no sign Iran is rebuilding its bombed nuclear sites?
questions.f: The IAEA head also said about 440kg of highly enriched uranium remains unaccounted for.

questions.q: Which AI company publicly filed its paperwork this week for a US sharemarket listing under the proposed ticker ANT?
questions.f: The S-1 filing landed on Monday 26 October US time and showed revenue of US$19.7 billion for the year to June.

questions.q: Apple unveiled its first touchscreen laptop this week. Which Mac line got it?
questions.f: The 14- and 16-inch models run M5 Pro or M5 Max chips and go on sale on 6 November.

questions.q: University of Bonn researchers found a REM-like sleep stage in which Australian creature?
questions.f: The species, Portia fimbriata, twitched its legs and moved its eyes during one of two distinct sleep stages.

questions.q: Blue Moon, one of the two lunar landers the Artemis III crew is set to test, is built by which company?
questions.f: NASA's Artemis III is planned for mid-2027, with crew working with both Blue Moon and SpaceX's Starship.

questions.q: ASIC told Senate estimates it is examining the collapse of Firmus's planned $44 billion float. What does Firmus build?
questions.f: The Tasmanian-based company calls its facilities 'AI factories' and pulled its ASX listing earlier in October.

questions.q: The US Federal Reserve held rates steady this week. Who chairs the Fed?
questions.f: The Fed kept its target range at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote, with two members preferring a hike.

questions.q: Microsoft's cloud computing platform grew revenue 48% in the latest quarter. What is it called?
questions.f: It was the first time Microsoft disclosed the platform's revenue in dollars: about US$33.2 billion.

questions.q: Senate estimates heard this week that the Snowy 2.0 hydro project is delayed again. What is its latest estimated cost?
questions.f: Officials also flagged another year's delay for the pumped-hydro scheme.

questions.q: Changes revealed at Senate estimates will cut second- and third-year places for which visa?
questions.f: Third-year places are falling sharply, from 31,000 to 5,000.

questions.q: Anthony Albanese is heading to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. Which Caribbean nation is hosting it?
questions.f: CHOGM runs from 1 to 4 November in St John's.

questions.q: At CHOGM, Albanese plans talks with the UK prime minister. Who holds that job?
questions.f: He took office in July 2026 after Keir Starmer stood down.

questions.q: By Monday, Brisbane had recorded about 170mm of rain for October. How does that compare with the month's average?
questions.f: Brisbane's October average is 87mm, and parts of the Sunshine Coast were heading for an October record.

questions.q: Legislation debated in the House this week would reserve up to what share of gas exports for domestic use?
questions.f: The government says it would boost supply for manufacturers and ease household gas prices.

questions.q: The resources minister called it 'unacceptable' that China-linked investors are defying orders to sell out of Perth's Northern Minerals. What does the company focus on?
questions.f: Canberra has ordered several China-linked shareholders to divest on national-interest grounds.

questions.q: Which Labor MP floated price caps on basics like bread and milk this week?
questions.f: The government pointed to the Grocery Code of Conduct and the ACCC instead, and the idea looks unlikely to go further.

questions.q: On what date next week are the US midterm elections held?
questions.f: Midterms fall on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

questions.q: Bulgaria's presidential race goes to a runoff on Sunday. Which candidate topped the first round?
questions.f: She won about 35% to Gyurov's 32% on a record-low turnout.

questions.q: Markets expect an RBA rate rise at next Tuesday's meeting. Which famous event falls on that same day?
questions.f: Markets were pricing about an 85% chance of a hike on 3 November after hot inflation figures.

questions.q: Australia's annual inflation rate for the year to September was announced this week. What was it?
questions.f: It was up from 4.0% in August, with housing and transport the biggest drivers.

questions.q: By how much did automotive fuel prices rise in September alone, according to the ABS?
questions.f: That followed a 14.8% jump in August, driven by higher world oil prices.

questions.q: What is the RBA's current cash rate, ahead of next week's decision?
questions.f: CBA expects a 25-basis-point rise to 4.85%.

questions.q: The Federal Court ordered Star Entertainment to pay what penalty for anti-money-laundering breaches?
questions.f: AUSTRAC had sought $400 million, and Star will pay in four instalments over 19 months.

questions.q: Brent crude was trading at roughly what price per barrel midweek?
questions.f: Higher oil prices have flowed through to Australian petrol bowsers and the inflation figures.

questions.q: Which former army chief's bloc challenged Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday's Israeli election?
questions.f: Neither bloc reached the 61 seats needed, so Netanyahu stays caretaker prime minister for now.

questions.q: Lula da Silva beat Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's runoff. Which term as president will this be for Lula?
questions.f: Lula, who turned 81 this week, won with just over 51% of the vote.

questions.q: Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat to a student-led movement in which country's parliamentary election?
questions.f: The student list was projected to win 135–140 of the parliament's 250 seats.

questions.q: Queensland's 'Breach Bail, Go to Jail' bill sets what minimum jail term for serious repeat offenders who reoffend on bail?
questions.f: The bill also makes breaching bail a standalone offence and toughens the bail test.

questions.q: Calls for fuel 'excise' relief continued in parliament this week. What is an excise?
questions.a: A tax on particular goods such as fuel or alcohol
questions.f: Excise is charged on certain domestically produced goods, with fuel excise one of the biggest earners.

questions.q: Benjamin Netanyahu stays on as 'caretaker' prime minister. What does caretaker mean here?
questions.a: Holding office temporarily until a new government forms
questions.f: Caretaker governments usually avoid major new decisions until a new government is formed.

questions.q: 'Embargo', a word often seen in trade news, comes from which language?
questions.f: It comes from the Spanish 'embargar', meaning to seize or restrain.

questions.q: The Ebola virus, back in the news this week, takes its name from what?
questions.f: It is named after the Ebola River in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

questions.q: Fire salamanders were found to glow green and cyan under UV light. Which spelling is correct?
questions.f: The word comes from fluorite, the mineral in which the effect was first studied.

questions.q: Brisbane had about 170mm of rain by Monday, against an October average of 87mm. How many millimetres above average is that?
Star must pay its $260 million penalty in four equal instalments. How many millions is each instalment?
Second-year working holiday places are being cut from 57,000 to 45,000. How many fewer places is that?
Kimi Antonelli leads the F1 title race with five Grands Prix left. At 25 points for a win, what's the most a driver can score from those five races (ignoring sprints)?
questions.f: 5 × 25 = 125, just two more than Antonelli's 123-point lead.

questions.q: Which horse won the 150th Cox Plate, the first one run at Flemington?
questions.f: The West Australian stayer, ridden by William Pike, collected the $4 million winner's prize.

questions.q: Who won Formula 1's United States Grand Prix in Austin?
questions.f: The 20-year-old Italian moved to the brink of his first world title, with Oscar Piastri seventh.

questions.q: Who scored a century in Australia's first innings of 429 in the third Test at Newlands?
questions.f: His 102 helped Australia to a 100-run first-innings lead in the series decider.

questions.q: Which team won a 12-inning World Series Game 4 to avoid being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers?
questions.f: Pinch-hitter Ben Williamson drove in the winning run in a 4–3 victory.

questions.q: 'Housewife' debuted at No. 1 on the ARIA singles chart. Who sings it?
questions.f: It's the Canadian singer's first ARIA No. 1 single.

questions.q: Fontaines D.C. debuted at No. 1 on the ARIA albums chart with Dopamine Chamber. Which country is the band from?
questions.f: Dopamine Chamber is the band's fifth studio album and also topped the UK chart.

questions.q: Which Australian act's album No Bad Memories debuted at No. 5 on the ARIA albums chart?
questions.f: The Rubens' Group Therapy debuted one place behind it, at No. 6.

questions.q: Clayface opened at No. 1 at the US box office. Which comic-book universe is it from?
questions.f: The DC Studios film took about US$24 million in its opening weekend.

questions.q: Nathan Fielder co-directed the documentary You Can See Everything, a box-office hit. Who is it about?
questions.f: The A24 film took US$19.5 million in its first weekend of wide release.

questions.q: The stop-motion fantasy Wildwood opened in US cinemas. Which animation studio made it?
questions.f: It was directed by Laika's CEO, Travis Knight, and opened with an 'A' CinemaScore.
